name: market-pay-first-campaign
about: A carrier with no history of its own, planned with market evidence: BLS pay for the state and the nation, and three facts read from competitors' job pages. The plan may cite them; it may write none of their figures.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.

BLS wage survey, 2025: heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers in Illinois, the state this ad's area is centred in, earned a median of $60,320 a year ($29.00 an hour); a tenth earned $39,710 or less and a tenth $86,300 or more.
BLS wage survey, 2025: heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers across the United States earned a median of $58,640 a year ($28.19 an hour); a tenth earned $40,140 or less and a tenth $79,380 or more.
A job page on prairieline-transport.example, saved by our recruiters, says (pay): They pay 62 to 70 cents per mile based on experience.
A job page on prairieline-transport.example, saved by our recruiters, says (sign-on bonus): They pay a $3,000 sign-on bonus over 90 days.
A job page on ridgecrest-hauling.example, saved by our recruiters, says (home time): Drivers are home every weekend, out Monday through Friday.

output.audience: Experienced Class A flatbed drivers who run or want regional Midwest lanes. Many may be at bigger fleets with less regular home time. A stated pay per mile, home weekly and an assigned truck at a small fleet would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile for regional flatbed work, stated as a plain rate.
angles.proof: The opening states a pay per mile.
angles.why: Pay is what drivers compare before anything else, and a nearby carrier's page gives a range by experience where this job states a rate. Nothing has been measured yet for this carrier.

angles.idea: Lead with being home weekly while running Midwest lanes, pictured on a home street.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: A competing flatbed page promises weekends home, so home time is what these drivers weigh. The job says home weekly only, so do not name days. No results measured yet.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck, shown as a flatbed rig parked and ready for its driver.
angles.proof: The job lists an assigned truck and flatbed work.
angles.why: Flatbed drivers care which truck they get, and an assigned truck is a concrete fact a picture can show. Untested: this carrier has no ad results yet.

angles.idea: Say plainly who this is for: Class A, the experience requirement, flatbed, Midwest lanes.
angles.proof: The job states Class A, an experience requirement, flatbed freight and Midwest lanes.
angles.why: No lead outcomes exist yet, so stating the requirement and the area up front guards against unqualified leads and against the benchmark's cost per lead line.

angles.idea: Set out the terms as a short list on a plain ground, closing on the small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.proof: The job holds the pay per mile, home weekly, the retirement plan and the small-fleet line.
angles.why: A new advertiser has no record to show, so the proof is the job's own stated terms. Nothing has been measured, so this tests whether facts alone draw leads.
